transcript.text: Potter. Tell us about a time during an operation — not the war, we've all read those books — an ordinary operation when you failed, and it was entirely your fault, and someone got hurt because of it. How did you handle it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It was my first year as an Auror. We were tracking a group of Death Eaters who were selling illegal enchantments to Muggle-borns. I was so eager to prove myself that I pushed ahead without consulting my team. We were ambushed, and an innocent Muggle was seriously injured. It was all my fault.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. And what was the nature of your eagerness, Potter? Was it a lack of trust in your team's abilities, or something else?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I wanted to show that I could handle the job. I was still proving myself, I suppose, after everything that had happened. I thought that by taking charge, I could demonstrate that I was up to the task. But I realize now that was a mistake. I should have trusted my team more.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Interesting. You say you should have trusted your team more. Yet you were the one who led the charge into the ambush. Did you consider the possibility that your team might have seen something you missed? Or were you simply too focused on your own need to prove something?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You're right. I was so focused on... on myself, that I didn't even think to look at the situation from anyone else's perspective. I... I didn't consider that my team might have noticed something I missed. It was a... a very稚拙的错误, wasn't it?

I felt like I'd failed in every possible way.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: And your team? Did you face them immediately after, or did you avoid them? I need to know how you handled the professional fallout, not just the personal guilt.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I wanted to hide. I felt like I had let everyone down. But I knew that wasn't an option. I faced my team, and... and I took full responsibility. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Standing by you is one thing, Potter. But did you learn? Or did you just learn to be more careful about when you charge ahead? There's a difference between controlling your impulses and understanding why they exist in the first place.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
